sources.name: kaikki.org Wiktextract — English (English Wiktionary edition)
sources.citation: Ylonen, T. (2022). Wiktextract: Wiktionary as Machine-Readable Structured Data. Proceedings of the 13th Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC), pp. 1395–1403. Data: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/ (Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL).
sources.notes: Wiktionary content under CC BY-SA 4.0 (and GFDL); used under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution to Wiktionary contributors and kaikki.org. Per-entry provenance is the word|pos key in sourceRefs.

sources.name: kaikki.org Wiktextract — Tiếng Anh (Vietnamese Wiktionary edition)
sources.citation: Ylonen, T. (2022). Wiktextract: Wiktionary as Machine-Readable Structured Data. Proceedings of the 13th Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC), pp. 1395–1403. Data: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/ (Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL).
sources.notes: Vietnamese Wiktionary content under CC BY-SA 4.0; the Vietnamese senses are the primary native glosses. Entries whose sense text only redirects ("Xem …") are skipped.

sources.name: FrequencyWords (OpenSubtitles 2018 word frequencies)
sources.citation: hermitdave/FrequencyWords — word frequency lists derived from OpenSubtitles2018 (content CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT). https://github.com/hermitdave/FrequencyWords
sources.notes: README: "MIT License for code, CC-by-sa-4.0 for content". Only the derived counts are used; per-million values are relative to the list total (documented in frequency-stats.json).

sources.name: wordfreq 3.1.1 (Zipf frequencies)
sources.citation: Speer, R. (2022). rspeer/wordfreq: v3.0 (v3.0.2). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7199437 — data CC BY-SA 4.0 (includes Google Books Ngram and SUBTLEX components; see the package README for their acknowledgements).
sources.notes: Exported at acquisition time by scripts/lexicon-etl/export-wordfreq.py from the pinned PyPI package (data CC BY-SA 4.0, code Apache-2.0); the export is `word,zipf` for the top 50,000 words of the `large` list when available. The author discourages dumps that strip attribution — the citation ships in ATTRIBUTIONS.md.

sources.name: CEFR-J Vocabulary Profile 1.5 (Tono Lab, TUFS) via Open Language Profiles
sources.citation: The CEFR-J Wordlist Version 1.5. Compiled by Yukio Tono, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. Retrieved via https://github.com/openlanguageprofiles/olp-en-cefrj (cefrj-vocabulary-profile-1.5.csv).
sources.notes: Terms of use (olp-en-cefrj README): "can be used for research and commercial purposes with no charge, provided that you cite the dataset properly"; copyright Tono Laboratory, TUFS. Used as a build-time selection anchor (level labels) only — no CEFR-J text ships.

notes: Lexicon ETL v2 (P3a) source manifest for en: every artifact is downloaded from its official location by the dispatch-only workflow .github/workflows/lexicon-source.yml (or a developer run of scripts/lexicon-etl.ts fetch), hashed, and pinned here; raw dumps are never committed. A retrieval that does not hash to the pin is source-version drift and extract refuses to run (re-pin deliberately with recon). Declared sources whose download could not be completed stay "not-retrieved" with the blocker recorded and can never be cited by a lexeme.
